title: Trust, Communication and Resilience in Cross-Cultural Organizational Systems: Insights from Industrial Relations Experts
content: Organizations increasingly operate in environments shaped by technological disruption, workforce diversity, organizational change, and persistent uncertainty. While resilience has become an important concern in contemporary organizations, industrial relations mechanisms continue to focus primarily on formal dialogue and conflict resolution, often overlooking relational and psychosocial dimensions. Although support groups are widely used in fields such as healthcare, psychology, and social work, their potential contribution to employment relations has received limited attention. This study explores how support groups may support organizational resilience, communication, and sustainable workplace relations. An exploratory qualitative approach was employed based on thirteen semi-structured interviews with experts from industrial relations, human resource management, trade unions, organizational management, higher education, healthcare, and economic research. The data were analysed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that participants viewed interpersonal relationships, open communication, and psychological safety as essential for effective workplace cooperation. They also identified limitations of traditional formal mechanisms in addressing workplace uncertainty and everyday relational challenges. Participants largely perceived support groups as complementary structures that can foster dialogue, collective learning, social cohesion, and adaptive capacity during periods of organizational change. The study contributes to extending the support group concept into the field of industrial relations and highlights its potential role in strengthening organizational resilience and social sustainability in increasingly uncertain environments.
